object_context: First strict regularity atom for the three-dimensional incompressible Navier–Stokes Millennium problem: explain whether the Leray energy class can be upgraded, using exact Navier–Stokes structure rather than generic energy cancellation, to a scale-critical a priori control strong enough to invoke a known regularity criterion before a first singular time.
structural_coordinates: equation on R^3 or the periodic 3-torus with viscosity nu>0 and divergence-free velocity
Navier–Stokes scaling u_lambda(x,t)=lambda u(lambda x,lambda^2 t), p_lambda=lambda^2 p(lambda x,lambda^2 t)
mixed velocity norm L_t^p L_x^q is scale critical when 2/p+3/q=1
the Leray energy class L_t^infinity L_x^2 intersect L_t^2 dot H_x^1 scales with exponent -1/2 and is supercritical
vorticity obeys partial_t omega + u dot grad omega = nu Delta omega + omega dot grad u, so three-dimensional stretching is the sign-indefinite production term absent in 2D
pressure is nonlocal through a Calderon-Zygmund relation and cannot be discarded in local regularity arguments
bounded L_t^infinity L_x^3 control is a critical endpoint regularity criterion, but energy bounds do not supply it
epsilon-regularity converts small scale-invariant local quantities into smoothness, but the root gap is obtaining such smallness uniformly from global data
concentration-compactness/rigidity can exclude blowup under bounded critical norms, but does not itself create the missing critical bound

generic energy cancellation plus broad harmonic-analysis estimates are insufficient in Tao's averaged Navier–Stokes model, so any successful positive route must exploit finer structure of the true bilinear nonlinearity
equivalent_formulations: derive an a priori bound in any established scale-critical Serrin/endpoint class from smooth finite-energy initial data
prove that a hypothetical first singular time forces a contradiction with an exact structure-derived critical quantity
upgrade global energy control into uniform epsilon-regularity at every concentration scale
show that every putative critical element/minimal blowup profile is impossible using a rigidity mechanism whose hypotheses follow from the energy class
find a scale-local geometric depletion law for vortex stretching strong enough to prevent critical concentration
solved_analogues: two-dimensional incompressible Navier–Stokes global regularity, where scalar vorticity has no vortex-stretching term
small-data global well-posedness in the critical BMO^{-1} framework of Koch–Tataru
near_solved_analogues: Caffarelli–Kohn–Nirenberg epsilon/partial regularity for suitable weak solutions
Kenig–Koch concentration-compactness plus rigidity under bounded critical dot H^{1/2} control
Barker–Prange quantitative regularity/concentration results under critical Type-I bounds

cross_domain_analogies.source_situation: A dissipative system with an amplifying feedback channel is stable when a dimensionless production-to-dissipation gain can be shown to stay below the threshold needed for runaway, often after choosing a representation that exposes the feedback loop.
common_abstraction: coercive dissipation competes with sign-indefinite nonlinear production
instability requires sustained gain across a nested sequence of smaller scales
a useful certificate must be dimensionless or scale compatible at the instability threshold
source_to_target_mapping: stored state/energy -> kinetic energy or localized critical quantity
damping -> viscous dissipation nu Delta u
feedback production -> vortex stretching omega dot grad u and associated nonlinear transfer
gain margin -> scale-local ratio/geometry describing how much stretching survives cancellation and dissipation
shared_constraints: the certificate must be evaluated on the actual evolving state, not an external forcing surrogate
the bound must compose across scales/times without assuming the desired regularity
a stability margin must survive worst-case admissible states
disanalogies: Navier–Stokes is an infinite-dimensional nonlocal PDE with no fixed finite-dimensional gain matrix
pressure and incompressibility couple spatial regions nonlocally
a control-theory analogy cannot supply an inequality or theorem without target-domain proof
cross_domain_analogies.proposed_principle: Before searching for another global energy inequality, expose the exact scale-local production-versus-dissipation feedback and ask whether true Navier–Stokes geometry forces a critical-scale gain deficit that the averaged blowup model does not share.
cross_domain_analogies.validation_obligation: Any retained gain/depletion quantity must be dimensionless under Navier–Stokes scaling, must be computable on smooth divergence-free test fields without using future regularity, must fail or change character for Tao-type averaged interactions, and must survive adversarial high-strain/vorticity-alignment configurations before it can support a theorem candidate.
cross_domain_analogies.provenance_note: Proposal-generation bridge from dissipativity/small-gain reasoning only; it creates no PDE authority.

analogy_scan_notes: Scanned 2D/critical-space/epsilon-regularity/concentration-compactness mathematics plus control/dissipativity and cascade-style analogies. Retained only the production-versus-dissipation feedback bridge because it has a direct scale-compatible mapping and an explicit falsification obligation. No everyday analogy was retained because none improved the exact PDE transfer map.
